name: Luba-Katanga (Kiluba)
notes: Luba-Katanga (Kiluba), Guthrie L.33, Bantu language of Haut-Katanga and Haut-Lomami provinces, DR Congo. 22-letter Latin alphabet: five vowels a/e/i/o/u (with a length contrast not marked in standard spelling) and 17 consonants. /p, b/ have the fricative allophones [ɸ, β] intervocalically or before a semivowel (Van Avermaet & Mbuya 1954). Prenasalized consonants (mb, nd, ng, nk, mp, nt, ns, nz, nj, mf, mv) are single phonemes, spelled as homorganic nasal+consonant digraphs. Tone is lexically and grammatically significant but unmarked in the standard orthography.

sources.author: Van Avermaet, E. & Mbuya, B.

sources.notes: Confirms intervocalic/pre-semivowel fricative allophony of b/p ([β]/[ɸ] between vowels, w, and y).

ancestors.notes: Luba branch of Bantu (Guthrie L.30), within Atlantic-Congo.

location.notes: Approximate centre of the Katanga/Lomami speaking area, DR Congo.
